tool.name: FAIRe2ENA: samples
tool.description: convert FAIRe sample metadata to ENA SAMPLE XML
tool.command: set -o pipefail; @LINK_INPUT@ python '$__tool_directory__/faire2ena_galaxy.py' sample --input_file input.xlsx --center_name '$center_name' #if $taxon.taxon_select == 'other': --taxon_id $taxon.taxon_id #else: --taxon_id $taxon.taxon_select #end if #if not $convert_dates: --no_date_conversion #end if --output_file '$samples_xml' --submission_file '$submission_xml' | tee '$log'

param.name: taxon_select
param.label: Sample taxon
param.help: ENA records environmental samples under a metagenome taxon. Choose the one that matches your water samples.

param.name: taxon_id
param.label: NCBI taxon ID
param.help: For example a more specific metagenome such as estuary or seawater metagenome. Search for it at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy

param.name: convert_dates
param.label: Convert eventDate values to a form ENA accepts
param.help: ENA rejects time zone offsets written as +hh:mm (e.g. 2021-09-14T11:00+08:00). With this on, such dates are converted to UTC (2021-09-14T03:00Z). With it off, the upstream script replaces them with 'not provided'.

has_n_elements_with_path.path: .//SAMPLE_ATTRIBUTE[TAG='sample volume or weight for DNA extraction']

has_text_matching.expression: 'nitrate' left out for 1 sample.*nitrate_unit is empty.*GOMECC4_BROWNSVILLE_Sta63_DCM_A
sample volume or weight for DNA extraction.*1 sample.*samp_vol_we_dna_ext_unit is empty.*GOMECC4_27N_Sta1_DCM_B
sample storage temperature.*1 sample.*not a number.*GOMECC4_BROWNSVILLE_Sta63_DCM_A

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool converts the **sampleMetadata** sheet of a FAIRe workbook into an ENA SAMPLE XML file, ready to register your samples with the `European Nucleotide Archive <https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena>`_. It also writes the SUBMISSION XML (action ADD) that ENA needs alongside it.
This is the first of two steps. Once ENA accepts the samples, it returns a **receipt** with an accession for each sample. Upload the receipt to Galaxy and use it in **FAIRe2ENA: experiments and runs**.
-----
**Inputs**
- **A FAIRe workbook** (.xlsx) with **projectMetadata** and **sampleMetadata** sheets. In sampleMetadata, the first two rows hold the requirement levels and sections, and row 3 holds the field names. The project_id in projectMetadata becomes the ENA *project name*. - **Your centre name**, as registered with your ENA Webin account. - **The sample taxon.** ENA files environmental samples under a metagenome taxon, and marine metagenome is the default.
**Outputs**
- **SAMPLE XML**: one SAMPLE for each row of sampleMetadata, with samp_name as its alias. - **SUBMISSION XML**: the action file to send with it. - **log**: messages from the conversion, including any fields that were filled with defaults.
-----
**Limitations**
- Samples are written against the ENA **water checklist (ERC000024)**. Soil, sediment and other sample types need a different checklist, and the tool does not support them yet. - Control samples (those whose samp_category is not *sample*) get "missing: control sample" for any mandatory fields that are empty, and their collection date becomes "not provided". - If a mandatory field is empty for a real sample and the script has no default for it, the tool stops and lists the samples and the FAIRe terms to fill in. - ENA wants temperature, salinity, storage temperature, sample size, extraction volume and the chemistry fields (oxygen, nutrients, carbon, chlorophyll and others) as plain numbers with a unit. The tool adds the units, from FAIRe's own units or the matching *_unit term (samp_size_unit, nitrate_unit and so on), converting where only a power of ten separates them (1540 mL of sample to 1.54 L, 0.5 µM nitrate to 0.5 µmol/L). A value that is not a number, or a size or volume with no unit, is left out and listed in the log; fill it in sampleMetadata and run the tool again to include it.
-----
**Submitting to ENA**
Test your submission on the ENA test server first, which deletes submissions after 24 hours. Download both XML files and submit them with the `Webin REST service <https://ena-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/submit/general-guide/programmatic.html>`_, for example::
curl --proto-default https -u Webin-XXXXX:PASSWORD \ -F "SUBMISSION=@submission.xml" -F "SAMPLE=@samples.xml" \ wwwdev.ebi.ac.uk/ena/submit/drop-box/submit/
For the real submission, use www.ebi.ac.uk in place of wwwdev.ebi.ac.uk. Save the XML that ENA returns, as this is the receipt the next tool needs.
